texts.li: {A_nameDef} has come to the council with a question that can't wait for the year to turn: which god does the colony honour this year? {GOD}, {GOD2}, or another? Whichever god is named, {A_pronoun} says, has its festival kept first and the most offerings carried to it this year.
A new year, and {A_nameDef} asks the council to name the god the colony will keep it for. {GOD} has carried us this far, {A_pronoun} says, but {GOD2} has been owed a year for a long time.
[lowtech] {A_nameDef} has laid out the god-stones by the fire and asks the council to choose one to carry through the year: {GOD}, {GOD2}, or another.
[priest] A year belongs to one god, {A_nameDef} keeps reminding everyone, and it's the priest's work to ask which. {GOD}, {GOD2}, or another?

li.label: Honour {GOD} this year
li.outcome: The council named {GOD} the colony's god for the year. {A_nameDef} said the words at {PLACE} that evening, and {GOD2}'s people went home quieter than they came.

li.label: Honour {GOD2} this year
li.outcome: The council named {GOD2} the colony's god for the year. Words were said that evening, and {GOD}'s people swore they would remember this.

li.label: Honour {GOD3} this year
li.outcome: The council named {GOD3} the colony's god for the year, to everyone's surprise. Words were said that evening.

texts.li: {A_nameDef} wants a temple for {GOD}: a room of its own around {PLACE}, fine enough that nobody walking in could mistake what it is for. {A_pronoun} would vow it to {GOD} before the council, and asks the colony to build it.
{A_nameDef} says {GOD} has been worshipped in a corner long enough. A temple, {A_pronoun} says, a proper room with walls and a door, and {A_pronoun} will vow it.
[lowtech] {A_nameDef} wants a house for {GOD}, with a roof over {PLACE} and good things on the walls, and will swear before the council to see it raised.

li.label: Raise a temple: {A_nameDef} vows it to {GOD}
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} vowed a temple to {GOD} before the council, and walked to {PLACE} that evening to say so there. The colony has a month to give {GOD} a fine room of its own.

li.label: {PLACE} will do as it is
li.outcome: The council said {PLACE} would do. {A_nameDef} went out to it alone and told {GOD} so.

li.why: the council kept {PLACE} as it was

li.label: Not now
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} took it well enough. Some say {GOD} took it less well.

li.why: the council put off a temple for {GOD}

texts.li: {A_nameDef} woke shaking and came straight to the council. {GOD} spoke in {A_possessive} dream, {A_pronoun} says, and asked for {PET_labelShort}, the finest beast the colony has. Give it, {A_pronoun} says, and the rain keeps coming; refuse, and {A_pronoun} is sure the sky will stay dry.
{A_nameDef} says {GOD} wants {PET_labelShort}. {A_pronoun} dreamt it three nights running: the beast walking out past the last field, and the sky dry as bone behind it if it doesn't.
[bonded] {A_nameDef} says {GOD} wants {PET_labelShort}, of all the beasts, and knows exactly whose heart that breaks. {GOD} was very clear, {A_pronoun} says. Give it, or the rain stays away.
[lowtech] {A_nameDef} read the bones and read them again. {GOD} wants {PET_labelShort} given to the wild, or no rain will come to the fields.

[step:believed] {A_nameDef} is sure of it: {GOD} wants {PET_labelShort} let go into the wild, and a dry spell will follow if the colony holds on to it. Half the council thinks it was a bad dream. The other half has seen what a dry spell does.

li.label: Give {PET_labelShort} to {GOD}
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} walked out to {PET_labelShort} and let it go. It went off toward the edge of the land at its own pace and didn't look back. Some say {GOD} was waiting for it there.

outcomes.li: [step:walking] {A_nameDef} let {PET_labelShort} go, and everyone saw where it went: straight to the edge of the land, as if called.

li.label: Refuse: the colony keeps {PET_labelShort}
li.outcome: The council kept {PET_labelShort}. {A_nameDef} looked at the sky the whole evening.

li.why: the colony refused {GOD} what was asked

li.label: Offer {GOD} something lesser at {PLACE}
li.outcome: The council sent a lesser gift to {PLACE} instead. {A_nameDef} said it was a gamble, and that {GOD} has been known to take a bargain.

li.why: a lesser gift in place of what was asked

texts.li: {A_nameDef} prays to {GOD}, {B_nameDef} to {GOD2}, and the stories say the two gods have never been able to stand each other. Now {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} can't either. Each wants the colony's next rite for their own god, and says the other god will take it as an insult.

{GOD} and {GOD2} are old rivals, and the colony has people of both. {A_nameDef} says {GOD} won't share a shrine's smoke with {GOD2}. {B_nameDef} says {GOD2} was here first. The council is asked to settle it.
[lowtech] There's one fire and two gods who hate each other. {A_nameDef} will tend it for {GOD}, {B_nameDef} for {GOD2}, and neither will step back.

li.label: {GOD} first
li.outcome: The council gave {GOD} the rite. {A_nameDef} said the words at {PLACE}. {B_nameDef} stayed away, and some say {GOD2} did too.

li.label: {GOD2} first
li.outcome: The council gave {GOD2} the rite. {B_nameDef} said the words. {A_nameDef} stayed away, and some say {GOD} did too.

li.label: Both, side by side
li.outcome: The council asked for one rite for both gods. {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} stood at opposite ends of it and said their own words. Neither god, some say, liked sharing.

li.why: made to share a rite with {GOD2}
made to share a rite with {GOD}
